entry.title: RawMod: Modification-Agnostic Detection of DNA Base Modifications from Nanopore Signal Pileups
entry.summary:
Summary: Identifying epigenetically modified bases (e.g., methylation) is crucial for many important applications such as discovering mechanisms of cancer development, cell differentiation, and bacterial defense. Nanopore sequencing generates electrical signals that can differentiate canonical bases from modified ones. To detect base modifications from signals, machine learning (ML) methods and statistical approaches are commonly used.

Source: bioRxiv Bioinformatics Preprints · Tags: #bioinformatics #genomics-proteins

entry.title: The Confessions of a Protein Language Model: Steering, Activations, and What Predicted Confidence Cannot Certify
entry.summary:
Protein generate-and-screen pipelines use interventions and readouts to select candidates, but rarely test whether these track their intended targets. We audit published repetition steering, ESMFold confidence, and an activation readout. Steering preserves confidence at its operating point, but a fitted cliff follows at alpha_50 = 1.240x (sweep's own control: 64.0%).

Source: bioRxiv Bioinformatics Preprints · Tags: #bioinformatics #genomics-proteins

entry.title: SubCellSeg: A generalist model for subcellular structure segmentation in 3D fluorescence microscopy
entry.summary:
Three-dimensional (3D) segmentation of subcellular structures from fluorescence microscopy images is the foundation of many analyses in quantitative cell biology. The prevailing approach addresses 3D segmentation one structure at a time, with a separate model trained for each structure type. By developing SubCellSeg, we demonstrate that a single model, trained jointly across a diverse range of structures, substantially and consistently outperforms structure-specific specialist models.

Source: bioRxiv Bioinformatics Preprints · Tags: #bioinformatics #genomics-proteins #distributed-systems

entry.title: Fast Pangenome Matching Statistics in Compressed Space with Move Structures
entry.summary:
Matching statistics and supermaximal exact matches (SMEMs) are key inputs for sequence homology search and classification. Methods such as MONI, PHONI, and ropebwt3 compute these statistics using compressed pangenome indexes, but are substantially slower than methods that compute approximations of matching statistics, such as pseudo-matching lengths (PMLs). PMLs can be computed quickly in a single pass, but SMEM computation can require overlapping forward or backward passes over the query.

Source: bioRxiv Bioinformatics Preprints · Tags: #bioinformatics #genomics-proteins

entry.title: scDeepSim: Deep Generative Simulation for Controlled Benchmarking of Single-Cell Methods
entry.summary:
Benchmarking single-cell computational methods requires both realistic data and reliable ground truth. However, annotating real datasets is costly and, even when available, may not fully represent the diverse settings where methods are used. Simulators address this gap by generating synthetic data that has fully specified ground truth and whose structure can be tailored to challenge competing methods.

Source: bioRxiv Bioinformatics Preprints · Tags: #bioinformatics #genomics-proteins #clean-tech #computer-vision

entry.title: RNA Small-Molecule Binding-Site Prediction by Integrating RNA Language Models and Structural Geometry
entry.summary:
RNAs are emerging as promising therapeutic targets, and small-molecule binding can modulate their structure and function, creating opportunities for therapeutic development. Accurate identification of RNA small-molecule binding sites is therefore important for understanding RNA-ligand interactions and facilitating RNA-targeted drug discovery. However, the structural complexity of RNA and the limited availability of experimentally characterized RNA-ligand complexes pose challenges for computational binding-site prediction.

Source: bioRxiv Bioinformatics Preprints · Tags: #bioinformatics #genomics-proteins #combinatorics

entry.title: Training reservoirs without looking back
entry.summary:
Nature Computational Science, Published online: 13 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s43588-026-01079-6 By training a reservoir computing system without access to its intermediate states and by eliminating the coupling between its nodes, a physical learning framework achieves efficient learning both in simulation and on optoelectronic hardware.

entry.title: Ab initio simulation of excited-state potential energy surfaces with transferable deep quantum Monte Carlo
entry.summary:
Nature Computational Science, Published online: 06 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s43588-026-01065-y Transferable deep-learning quantum Monte Carlo for molecular excited states is introduced. Sharing parameters, an ansatz represents the wavefunction across molecular geometries and states, reducing the cost of modeling potential energy surfaces.

Source: Nature Computational Science · Tags: #bioinformatics #materials-science
